transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-21
Start: 2027-03-21T16:00:00-07:00
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE); Maya Lin (Redwood SE); John Park (CTO, Celero); Priya Desai (ML Engineer); Sam Okoro (Infra Lead, Celero)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial): Quick run through of current infra, desired p95 targets (100ms for short chat, 500ms for longer streaming), planned concurrency (up to 200 concurrent users, batching expected), and next steps to run token/second benchmarking.

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE, with Maya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] John: Good, thanks. Busy week but ready to dive in.
[00:10] Priya: Hi, yea thanks. We sent a short doc earlier with our traffic profile.
[00:15] Maya: Got it, we pulled that in — looks useful, thanks. Today we want to understand your latency SLOs, concurrency, and whether hosted fits or we should talk dedicated/private.
[00:25] Sam: Right now we're running a mix of in-house microservices and a small cluster for model hosting. Primary concern is p95 under load; we need predictable sub-200ms for our short responses and streaming for long-form receipts.
[00:38] Alex: Great, can you quantify concurrency and token rates? e.g. how many requests/sec and average tokens per request?
[00:44] Priya: Peak concurrent users around 180-200, but requests are bursty. Average prompt is 80 tokens, completion about 120 tokens. We estimated needing roughly 40k tokens/sec at peak.
[00:55] Maya: 40k tokens/sec is a solid number; depending on model/quantization that'll change. For hosted we can route across pools; for dedicated you get reserved GPU capacity for more consistent p95.
[01:10] John: We're leaning hosted to start because of time to market but if p95s slip we need an option to go dedicated or private VPC. Security is also big — SOC 2, KMS, SSO.
[01:22] Alex: Totally. We support SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integrations, audit logs, and private control plane for VPC. We'll share the compliance pack after the call.
[01:30] Priya: On latency we care a lot about streaming. Many of our responses are partial and we'd like first-byte p95 < 150ms and end-to-end p95 < 500ms for long receipts. Is that something Redwood can guarantee?
[01:45] Maya: We aim for p95 SLOs per model and route. Hosted has good latency for most open models — we've benchmarked down to 80-120ms first byte with smaller context. For streaming long sequences it's often bound by token generation speed — that is tokens/sec from the model. We do batching and KV cache to improve.
[02:05] Sam: Tell me more about the KV cache — is that prefix caching? How does it work with user sessions?
[02:12] Maya: Yes it's prefix/K-V cache; sometimes transcripts will show as KV cash, sorry the transcript generator hates that word — it's K-V cache. We cache past key/value states for repeated prefixes so repeat calls with similar context skip recompute. That helps with p95 for short-turn reuse.
[02:30] John: What about quantization? We use a mix of LLMs, some quantized to int8 for cost. Does Redwood support quantized kernels?
[02:36] Maya: Yes, runtime supports quantization-friendly execution paths — int8 and newer 4-bit variants. Kernel selection is automatic based on model arch and HW. For dedicated we can tune kernels for your workload.
[02:50] Priya: For benchmarking, we want to mimic our real prompt set including streaming tokens. Can you run a token/sec test with our prompts and measure p95 under 200 concurrent simulated users?
[02:59] Alex: Yes, we can provision a benchmark run. We'll need the prompt set and a traffic profile. Maya will set up a test harness — it'll report tokens/sec, latency p50/p95, and throughput.
[03:12] Priya: We'll share the CSV by tomorrow.
[03:15] Sam: On network — latency from our region matters. We need region-based routing; if hosted can't meet our latency we may prefer Dedicated in a nearby region or Private on-prem for strict compliance.
[03:27] Maya: We support regional routing and can pin deployments. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs in a region; Private gives full on-prem or VPC control. Each has tradeoffs: hosted = fastest onboarding, dedicated = predictable tail-latency, private = max control + compliance.
[03:42] John: Can you talk about autoscale and burst capacity? We have diurnal + marketing spikes.
[03:48] Alex: Hosted auto-scales and we can configure burst capacity for spikes. Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies and burst options but needs commit sizing. We'll show typical latency vs throughput charts in the pricing deck.
[03:58] Priya: How does batching affect streaming? If requests are batched we might increase latency for first-byte.
[04:04] Maya: Right — continuous batching improves tokens/sec and overall cost but can add small client-perceived latency. For streaming-first-byte SLOs we configure low-latency queues and smaller batch windows; it's a knob. Also caching avoids recompute so batching less necessary for repeated prefixes.
[04:20] John: Any public benchmarks you can share? We looked at your docs but want apples-to-apples vs Anthropic/OpenAI.
[04:27] Alex: We'll share our benchmark spreadsheet and a sample reproducible harness. Keep in mind models, quantization, and prompt length all matter. We'll run a Celero-specific benchmark so you get apples-to-apples.
[04:36] Sam: For security, we need KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that done for hosted?
[04:44] Maya: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS, and audit logs can be exported to your workspace. Private gives even more control but hosted covers common enterprise needs.
[04:54] Priya: For SLOs, can you commit to any p95 numbers for hosted or is that only for dedicated?
[05:00] Alex: Hosted has informal SLOs but for contractual SLOs we typically use Dedicated with SLA-backed uptime/latency targets. We can propose a pilot with success criteria and ramp to dedicated if needed.
[05:12] John: Pricing — curious about token-based pricing vs dedicated commit. We'll need both numbers to evaluate TCO.
[05:19] Alex: We'll include per-token hosted pricing plus dedicated commit tiers and example cost models for your 40k tokens/sec peak to estimate run-rate.
[05:28] Maya: A note on model fallbacks: we support routing to cheaper or lower-latency variants if primary capacity is constrained. That helps keep p95s predictable during spikes.
[05:40] Priya: Great. For the benchmark, please include metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency for first-byte and end-to-end, GPU utilization, and estimated cost per 1M tokens.
[05:53] Maya: Will do. We'll capture token/sec and break down latency by generation vs network.
[06:01] John: Will you also simulate concurrency patterns? Our traffic is very bursty — sudden 5x spikes forminutes.
[06:07] Alex: Yes we'll run both steady-state and spike tests. For spike tests we'll examine tail-latency and route fallback behavior.
[06:15] Sam: Anything else we should know about integrating with our stack? We use GCP, and we want private VPC peering if we go private.
[06:22] Maya: We support GCP regions and VPC peering for Private. For hosted we'll try to keep nodes in the same region with low egress. We'll share network requirements doc.
[06:31] Priya: On model choices, we're evaluating a trimmed open Llama variant and a mid-size MPT for embeddings. Any recommendations?
[06:38] Maya: For latency/cost balance, smaller quantized variants often perform best for interactive experiences. We'll suggest models and quant profiles based on your prompt hist. We'll include those recommendations in the follow-up.
[06:52] John: Ok, sounds good. Let's run the benchmark and reconvene after results. Can we do a technical deep dive with infra folks?
[06:59] Alex: Yes, Maya will lead the deep dive. We'll aim for the week of 3/28.
[07:05] Priya: I'll coordinate schedules and share the prompts.
[07:08] Alex: Quick recap before we close: 1) Alex sends pricing + benchmark proposal, 2) Maya schedules deep-dive and provisions test harness, 3) Celero shares prompt set and traffic CSV. Any other open items?
[07:20] John: Not from me.
[07:23] Sam: Nope.
[07:25] Priya: All good.
[07:27] Alex: Great thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites.
[07:30] End of recording.

Notes: transcription has occasional name/term errors (e.g., K-V cash instead of KV cache, SAML sometimes transcribed S-A-M-L). References to shared artifacts: pricing deck (link to be sent), compliance pack (link), benchmark harness (link).
